def decide(bars, account):
    closes = bars["close"]
    n = len(closes)
    if n < 155:
        return "HOLD", "not enough history for 150-day average"
    ma150 = sum(closes[-150:]) / 150
    ma150_prev = sum(closes[-155:-5]) / 150
    ma50 = sum(closes[-50:]) / 50
    price = closes[-1]
    rising = ma150 > ma150_prev
    if account["position"] <= 0:
        if price > ma50 and price > ma150 and rising:
            return "BUY", "close above 50d and rising 150d average"
        return "HOLD", "no entry signal"
    if price < ma150 * 0.95:
        return "SELL", "close more than 5% below 150-day average"
    return "HOLD", "holding within trend band"

v001seed · written 2024-11-01 (2024-W44) · parent -live 2024-11-01 → 2025-07-25 (180 sessions): -21.39% vs buy & hold -10.03% (alpha -11.36 pp)
Starting strategy supplied by the researcher and identical for every run; you did not write it. It is deliberately simple. Judge it on the evidence like any other version.
def decide(bars, account):
    """Seed strategy: hold the stock while its close is above the 20-day average."""
    closes = bars["close"]
    if len(closes) < 20:
        return "HOLD", "not enough history for a 20-day average"
    average = sum(closes[-20:]) / 20
    price = closes[-1]
    if account["position"] <= 0 and price > average:
        return "BUY", "close is above the 20-day average"
    if account["position"] > 0 and price < average:
        return "SELL", "close is below the 20-day average"
    return "HOLD", "no change"
